scope: Six new Byzantine works and one existing work date review; all remain in review.

items.title: Geoponica
date: The matched source identifies the tenth-century compilation, not its earlier source collection or surviving manuscript dates.
items.description: A twenty-book Byzantine compendium of farming, animals, crops and rural knowledge, preserving material from earlier agricultural writers.
items.identityReview: The tenth-century work was compiled for Constantine VII. The source explicitly rejects attribution of this compilation to Cassianus Bassus; his earlier material was incorporated into it. Wikidata P407 records Ancient Greek.

items.title: Chronicon Paschale
date: The matched source places composition in the seventh century, probably in the last decade of Heraclius’s reign. The broad century preserves uncertainty; events covered and later manuscript dates are not composition dates.
items.description: A Christian world chronicle that joins historical events to biblical chronology and the calculation of Easter.
items.basis: Byzantine historical writing and Christian chronology.
items.identityReview: The compiler is unidentified. Medieval Greek is directly recorded in P407; no speculative personal identity is linked.

items.title: Basilika
date: The matched article gives completion around 892. Its reviewed composition date takes precedence over the conflicting, unreferenced Wikidata publication year 888.
items.description: A sixty-book reworking of Roman law in Greek, commissioned under Leo VI to make the inherited legal tradition usable in Byzantium.
items.basis: Byzantine legal compilation and transmission of Roman law.
items.identityReview: Greek is directly recorded in P407 and discussed in the article. Imperial commission is not treated as personal authorship.

items.title: Book of the Eparch
date: Date not established · layers from the reigns of Leo VI and Nikephoros II

Traditionally associated with Leo VI (886–912), but the source describes gradual accumulation and a final form no earlier than Nikephoros II (963–969). No defensible closed composition interval is established here, so both years remain unknown.
items.description: Regulations for trades and guilds in Constantinople, revealing how the city supervised markets, production, prices and professional life.
items.identityReview: Work identity is Book of the Prefect/Eparch. Greek original is evidenced by the article’s Greek title and original-text discussion; no modern translation language or editor is used.

items.title: Ecloga (Ekloge ton nomon)
date: The source reports competing adoption dates of 726 and 741. These are alternative proposals, not a claim of continuous composition across the interval.
items.description: A concise Byzantine legal code adapting Roman law to contemporary civil and criminal cases, written in Greek for practical use.
items.basis: Byzantine legal reform under the Isaurian dynasty.
items.identityReview: The article explicitly states that the code was written in Greek. Leo III and Constantine V are imperial sponsors, not inferred individual authors.

items.title: Belthandros and Chrysantza
date: The original romance is probably thirteenth- or fourteenth-century, with later fifteenth-century reworking. The interval is a broad estimate for the original, not the date of the surviving sixteenth-century manuscript.
items.description: An anonymous verse romance following Belthandros and Chrysantza through love, separation and trials in a world blending Byzantine and chivalric traditions.
items.basis: Vernacular Byzantine fiction alongside historical and legal works.
items.identityReview: Anonymous authorship and vernacular Greek are explicit in the article; Medieval Greek is also directly recorded in P407.

date: The matched author article explicitly dates the Hexabiblos to 1344–1345 and distinguishes its first printing in 1540.
items.basis: Byzantine legal literature and its later Balkan reception.
items.identityReview: Q6649850 is the work, distinct from its author Q769438. Source is the author article’s explicit description of this book.
